title: India's Buying Intent Falls to 19-Month Low Days Before Diwali
excerpt: TRA's Buying Intent Index dropped 3.96% to 94.31 in October 2026, with 16 of 23 categories contracting — even as healthcare and food buying intent rose sharply ahead of the November 8 festival.
body:
• India's Buying Intent Index (BII), published by TRA, fell 3.96% in October 2026 to 94.31 — its lowest reading in 19 months, after four consecutive months of decline.
  • 16 of the 23 super-categories tracked by the index contracted in October; Telecom (-20.33%), Stationery (-17.87%), Services (-17.53%) and Retail (-17.42%) fell steepest.
  • Healthcare (+34.86%) and Food & Beverage (+12.45%) were the strongest gainers — Indian Pharmaceuticals buying intent rose 74.3%.
  • For readers buying for family in India this Diwali — Sunday, November 8, 2026 — intent is weakest for phones and home appliances after months of declines; TRA's November reading will show whether festive demand recovered.

Indian consumers are heading into Diwali in an unusually cautious mood. India's Buying Intent Index, the monthly measure of purchase readiness published by TRA, fell to 94.31 in October 2026, according to Social Samosa's report on the index — the lowest reading in 19 months, below the previous low of 94.94 recorded in January 2026. Storyboard18, reporting the same TRA release, put the monthly fall at 3.96% and noted the index was also lower than its level a year earlier.

The timing is what makes the reading striking. The October figure was recorded six days before Diwali, normally the peak of India's consumer calendar. In 2025, when Diwali fell on October 20, the national index rose 2.9% to 100.16 — its highest reading in the series. This year, Diwali falls on November 8, and the index has fallen for four consecutive months instead of rising into the festival.

"India's Buying Intent Index has reached its lowest point in 19 months, and October has recorded the steepest monthly fall in the series."

— TRA Buying Intent Index report, October 2026

Weakness Is Broad, and Durables Are the Soft Spot

The decline extended across 16 of the 23 super-categories the index tracks. The weakness had been building for months: seven of the 10 largest super-categories declined between July and September, including FMCG (-19.6%), Food & Beverage (-16.6%), Personal Accessories (-11.8%) and Consumer Electronics (-8.2%). By October, nine of the 10 largest were below their July readings, led by FMCG (-23.6%), Retail (-19.5%), Personal Accessories (-15.1%) and Consumer Electronics (-13.7%).

Consumer durables entered the Diwali period after sustained declines. Mobile Phones recorded four consecutive months of falling buying intent, while Air Conditioners, Refrigerators and Washing Machines each recorded three consecutive monthly falls — a sequence none of the four categories showed in October 2025. For households in India weighing a big-ticket festive purchase, and for diaspora families funding one, the data points to deferral rather than a spending spree.

Healthcare and Food Buck the Trend

Two areas moved sharply the other way. Healthcare buying intent rose 34.86% in October, with Indian Pharmaceuticals up 74.3%, and private health insurance maintained buying intent at several times its 2025 levels for a fifth consecutive month. Food & Beverage rose 12.45%, even though it had declined over the July–September period. The pattern suggests households are prioritising health cover and festive food over discretionary durables — spending where it feels essential, pausing where it does not.

Banking and financial services told a mixed story. The BFSI super-category declined 10.11% in October, yet within it, HDFC Bank recorded a 19-month high reading of 967.6, while Axis Bank registered a third consecutive monthly fall.

Brand Leaders Shuffle

The October readings also reshuffled category leaders. In Passenger Vehicles, Tata Motors led for the seventh time in eight months with a reading of 946.6, ahead of Hyundai (597.4) and Maruti Suzuki (595.5) — the widest lead recorded by any category leader since June 2025. In Metals, JSW Steel overtook Tata Steel for the first time in the 19-month series, ending Tata Steel's 18-month run at the top. Vivo led Mobile Phones for a fourth consecutive month, following Apple iPhone's seven-month run from April to October 2025.

What to Watch

The index measures intent, not completed purchases, and intent recorded before the festival can still convert into late buying. TRA's November reading will provide the corresponding festive-month observation and, in the report's own words, November and December will complete the picture for 2026. For diaspora readers, the practical read is narrow but useful: if you are planning a phone, appliance or vehicle purchase for family in India this Diwali, you are shopping in a market where demand has been softening for four straight months — and the definitive festive verdict arrives with the November index.
